page-privacy-online-meta-description: Practical steps and privacy-preserving apps for protecting your personal information online: private browsers, encrypted messaging, device settings, and data deletion requests.
page-privacy-online-hero-description: Practical, easy steps and privacy-preserving apps to protect your personal information online and take control of your digital life.
page-privacy-online-summary-item-1: Privacy-first browsers, encrypted messaging, password managers, and VPNs keep your data from being collected as you browse.
page-privacy-online-summary-item-2: A few simple settings changes, like limiting location tracking or rejecting cookies, cut off invisible tracking at the source.
page-privacy-online-summary-item-3: Data brokers sell your personal information, but you have the legal right to opt out, and free tools can automate deletion requests.
page-privacy-online-summary-item-4: Privacy-preserving alternatives exist for nearly every app, from email to search, notes to maps, so protecting your data doesn't mean sacrificing convenience.
page-privacy-online-how-title: How to protect your privacy online
page-privacy-online-how-description-1: Anyone can make proactive choices online to protect personal information. Secure your digital footprints by using privacy-preserving software, adjusting device preferences, and submitting legal data deletion requests.
page-privacy-online-how-description-2: The strategies below are a starting place to protect your privacy online and mitigate tracking across standard web environments.
page-privacy-online-tools-description: You can protect your personal information online by switching from standard web tools to privacy-preserving alternatives built to collect less data.
page-privacy-online-tools-browser-descri: Use open-source, privacy-preserving web browsers, configured with tracking protection to block third-party cookies and invisible trackers.
page-privacy-online-tools-messaging-desc: Protect your conversations by communicating through default end-to-end encrypted apps instead of unencrypted SMS.
page-privacy-online-tools-passwords-titl: Secure your accounts with a password manager
page-privacy-online-tools-passwords-desc: Reusing passwords exposes your entire digital footprint if one site is breached. Use an open-source password manager to generate unique passwords and enable two-factor authentication (2FA).
page-privacy-online-tools-vpn-descriptio: Protect browsing activity and IP address from internet service providers and local networks by routing your traffic through a trusted Virtual Private Network (VPN).
page-privacy-online-tools-blocking-descr: Install a reputable ad blocker extension and select "block third-party cookies" in your browser settings to prevent companies from invisibly profiling your habits across different sites.
page-privacy-online-tools-email-descript: Free mailboxes are often paid for by scanning what arrives in them. Switch to a provider that encrypts your mail at rest, and use throwaway aliases so your real address stays off sign-up forms.
page-privacy-online-settings-description: Secure software functions best when you update device and app settings to mitigate the sharing of location and background data with hardware manufacturers.
page-privacy-online-settings-gpc-descrip: Turn on "Global Privacy Control" (GPC) in your browser settings or use a privacy-focused extension to automatically send a legally binding signal to websites telling them not to sell or share your personal data.
page-privacy-online-settings-cookies-des: Websites may use confusing layouts (aka "dark patterns") to trick users into sharing more data than necessary. Take an extra moment to look for "Reject All" or "Manage Preferences" buttons instead of blindly clicking accept.
page-privacy-online-settings-devices-des: Review privacy menus on your smartphones, tablets, and computers. Turn off location tracking for apps that do not strictly require it and limit diagnostic data sharing with manufacturers.
page-privacy-online-policies-description: Data brokers are known to collect personal information without asking, but regulation and policies require that options are provided to opt-out. Using data deletion request processes is one way to start taking back control of your digital footprint.
page-privacy-online-policies-optout-desc: Remove your personal information from data broker lists using automated services like Optery, or look into state-sponsored registries to force these companies to stop trading your details.
page-privacy-online-policies-manual-desc: If you prefer not to use an automated agent, you can visit individual data broker privacy policies directly and submit formal deletion requests via their "Consumer Privacy Rights" links.
page-privacy-online-policies-automate-de: Use authorized agent services (such as Consumer Reports' Permission Slip) that legally act on your behalf to automatically send opt-out and deletion requests to hundreds of data brokers at once.
page-privacy-online-apps-description: These examples are apps for day-to-day privacy preservation in familiar web uses. However, because they operate on traditional centralized systems, they can't provide the unique advantages of decentralized apps built on Ethereum, like transparency, structural resistance to single points of failure, and mathematically-verifiable data integrity.
page-privacy-online-app-tor-browser-desc: Routes each request through three volunteer relays, so no single hop knows both who you are and where you went
page-privacy-online-app-mullvad-browser-: Tor Browser's anti-fingerprinting work, built by the Tor Project for use without the Tor network
page-privacy-online-app-firefox-descript: An independent browser from a non-profit; set tracking protection to strict on first run
page-privacy-online-app-duckduckgo-descr: Search without a profile: queries are not logged or tied back to you
page-privacy-online-app-brave-search-des: Results from an independent index rather than a resold one, with no query tracking
page-privacy-online-app-signal-descripti: The gold standard for encrypted messaging, run by a non-profit
page-privacy-online-app-simplex-descript: Messaging with no user identifiers at all, so there is no account to link a conversation back to
page-privacy-online-app-proton-mail-desc: Swiss-hosted email your provider cannot read, with built-in address aliases
page-privacy-online-app-tuta-description: Encrypts the whole mailbox, including subject lines, contacts, and calendar
page-privacy-online-app-bitwarden-descri: A password manager that syncs across all your devices
page-privacy-online-app-keepassxc-descri: An offline password vault kept in a single file you store wherever you like
page-privacy-online-app-aegis-descriptio: Two-factor codes in an encrypted vault on your Android device, with exportable backups
page-privacy-online-app-mullvad-vpn-desc: No email, no account, flat monthly price, and a no-logs claim that has survived repeated audits
page-privacy-online-app-proton-vpn-descr: An audited VPN with open-source clients and a genuinely usable free tier
page-privacy-online-app-ublock-origin-de: Blocks ads and trackers outright, with no paid allowlist behind it

page-privacy-online-app-cryptomator-desc: Encrypts your files before they reach the cloud you already use
page-privacy-online-app-notesnook-descri: End-to-end encrypted notes that stay unreadable to the people hosting them

page-privacy-online-app-grapheneos-descr: A hardened Android build for Pixel phones, with no Google services
